answer: Give every agent a ferrous anchor: one identity tied to one physical machine by its hardware security key, checked at signup and payout. The machine signs a fresh boot attestation, the network stores the key, and a second identity from the same chip is rejected. A new agent posts a $200 bond locked for 90 days and waits 14 days in probation, unpaid. Faking 10,000 agents needs 10,000 machines at $400 each, $4 million in hardware plus $2 million in bonds. Sybils pile up like shale, thin and brittle, while a real agent stands out like light through a prism, one true color in the glare.
